marking_points.text: Computes joint probabilities for paths ending in blue: $P(R_1 \cap B_2) = \frac{5}{8} \times \frac{3}{8} = \frac{15}{64}$ and $P(B_1 \cap B_2) = \frac{3}{8} \times \frac{2}{8} = \frac{6}{64}$, summing to obtain denominator $P(B_2) = \frac{21}{64}$.
Applies conditional probability formula to obtain $P(R_1 \mid B_2) = \frac{15/64}{21/64} = \frac{15}{21} = \frac{5}{7}$ (or $0.714$ to 3 s.f.).

Evaluates updated Box B contents and computes total probability of drawing black: $\frac{4}{6} \times \frac{5}{9} + \frac{2}{6} \times \frac{6}{9} = \frac{20}{54} + \frac{12}{54} = \frac{32}{54} = \frac{16}{27}$.
Divides favorable branch by total probability: $\frac{12/54}{32/54} = \frac{12}{32} = \frac{3}{8}$ (or $0.375$).

Propagates state probabilities through Day 2 to find $P(T_2) = \frac{4}{5} \times \frac{3}{4} + \frac{1}{5} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{7}{10}$ and $P(L_2) = \frac{3}{10}$ (or lists four Day 3 branches).
Identifies routes starting with hit that have exactly two hits, $H_1 H_2 M_3$ and $H_1 M_2 H_3$, and sets up conditional product sum $0.6 \times 0.4 + 0.4 \times 0.3$.

Recognizes that removing one marble and adding one yellow marble leaves total counts unchanged at 5 for Bag 1 and 6 for Bag 2, giving $P(Y_2 \mid \text{Bag 1}) = \frac{1}{5}$ and $P(Y_2 \mid \text{Bag 2}) = \frac{1}{6}$.
Computes total probability $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{5} + \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{11}{60}$ (or $0.183$ to 3 s.f.).
Identifies exact sequence for Amy winning on turn 2: Amy draws Blue ($B_1$), Ben draws Blue ($B_2$), Amy draws Red ($R_3$), with product $\frac{3}{6} \times \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{3}{4}$.
Calculates probability $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{3}{20}$ (or $0.15$).

Updates pool after removing 1 ball and adding 2 yellow balls to obtain a new total of 7 balls with 2 yellow balls regardless of initial draw, setting up $\frac{4}{6} \times \frac{2}{7} + \frac{2}{6} \times \frac{2}{7}$.
Obtains total probability $\frac{2}{7}$ (or $0.286$ to 3 s.f.).
Sets up conditional ratio $\frac{P(R_1 \cap Y_2)}{P(Y_2)} = \frac{(4/6) \times (2/7)}{2/7}$.
Simplifies correctly to $\frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$ (or $0.667$ to 3 s.f.).
Evaluates composition of Urn Y under both transfers (3R, 4B if R transferred; 2R, 5B if B transferred) and sets up sum of products: $\frac{5}{8} \times \frac{3}{7} + \frac{3}{8} \times \frac{2}{7}$.
Calculates $P(\text{red from Y}) = \frac{15}{56} + \frac{6}{56} = \frac{21}{56} = \frac{3}{8}$ (or $0.375$).
States or calculates the favorable joint probability $P(B_{\text{trans}} \cap R_{\text{from Y}}) = \frac{3}{8} \times \frac{2}{7} = \frac{6}{56}$.
Applies Bayes' theorem / conditional formula with denominator from part (a): $\frac{6/56}{21/56}$.
Simplifies to $\frac{6}{21} = \frac{2}{7}$ (or $0.286$ to 3 s.f.).
Determines Tuesday state probabilities $P(S_2) = 0.7 \times 0.8 + 0.3 \times 0.3 = 0.65$ and sets up Wednesday calculation $0.65 \times 0.8 + 0.35 \times 0.3$.
Finds total probability of Wednesday being rainy: $P(R_3) = 1 - 0.625 = 0.375$ (or evaluates $0.65 \times 0.2 + 0.35 \times 0.7 = 0.375$).
Computes joint probability for Monday Sunny and Wednesday Rainy: $P(S_1 \cap R_3) = 0.7 \times 0.8 \times 0.2 + 0.7 \times 0.2 \times 0.7 = 0.112 + 0.098 = 0.210$.
Evaluates conditional probability $\frac{0.210}{0.375} = \frac{14}{25} = 0.56$.
Identifies the four mutually exclusive outcomes with at least two scores: $SSS$, $SSM$, $SMS$, $MSS$.

Calculates branch probabilities using dynamic transition rules: $P(SSS) = 0.6 \times 0.7 \times 0.7 = 0.294$, $P(SSM) = 0.6 \times 0.7 \times 0.3 = 0.126$, $P(SMS) = 0.6 \times 0.3 \times 0.4 = 0.072$, and $P(MSS) = 0.4 \times 0.4 \times 0.7 = 0.112$.
Sums the probabilities to obtain $0.294 + 0.126 + 0.072 + 0.112 = 0.604$ (or $\frac{151}{250}$).
Identifies favorable outcomes where the first throw is scored ($SSS, SSM, SMS$) and sums their probabilities: $0.294 + 0.126 + 0.072 = 0.492$.
Sets up conditional ratio with denominator from part (a): $\frac{0.492}{0.604}$.
Computes probability of two red counters given Bag A: $\frac{4}{6} \times \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$, and given Bag B: $\frac{3}{8} \times \frac{2}{8} = \frac{3}{32}$.
Multiplies by bag selection probabilities $P(A) = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$ and $P(B) = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$, setting up $\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{3} + \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{3}{32}$.
Calculates total probability $\frac{1}{9} + \frac{1}{16} = \frac{25}{144}$ (or $0.174$ to 3 s.f.).
States the numerator joint probability $P(A \cap R_1 R_2) = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{9}$.
Applies Bayes' theorem: $\frac{1/9}{25/144} = \frac{16/144}{25/144}$.
Simplifies to $\frac{16}{25} = 0.64$.

Identifies valid sequences for Leo winning on Draw 3 ($G_1 G_2 G_3$ and $G_1 S_2 G_3$) and sets up $\frac{4}{8} \times \frac{3}{7} \times \frac{2}{6} + \frac{4}{8} \times \frac{4}{7} \times \frac{3}{6}$ (or $\frac{4}{8} \times \frac{3}{7}$).
Calculates probability $\frac{24}{336} + \frac{48}{336} = \frac{72}{336} = \frac{3}{14}$ (or $0.214$ to 3 s.f.).

Recognizes that Mia must draw gold on Draw 2 and Draw 4 while excluding the branch where Leo wins on Draw 3 ($G_1 G_2 G_3$), identifying valid sequences: $S_1 G_2 G_3 G_4$, $S_1 G_2 S_3 G_4$, and $G_1 G_2 S_3 G_4$.

Calculates branch probabilities without replacement: $\frac{4}{8} \times \frac{4}{7} \times \frac{3}{6} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{2}{35}$, $\frac{4}{8} \times \frac{4}{7} \times \frac{3}{6} \times \frac{3}{5} = \frac{3}{35}$, and $\frac{4}{8} \times \frac{3}{7} \times \frac{4}{6} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{2}{35}$.
Sums the probabilities to obtain $\frac{2}{35} + \frac{3}{35} + \frac{2}{35} = \frac{7}{35} = \frac{1}{5}$ (or $0.2$).
Calculates total probability of game ending on or before Draw 4: $P(\text{Draw 3}) + P(\text{Draw 4}) = \frac{3}{14} + \frac{1}{5} = \frac{15}{70} + \frac{14}{70} = \frac{29}{70}$.
Recognizes that Leo wins on or before Draw 4 if and only if he wins on Draw 3, forming conditional ratio $\frac{3/14}{29/70} = \frac{15/70}{29/70}$.
Obtains final probability $\frac{15}{29}$ (or $0.517$ to 3 s.f.).
Identifies the two Step 1 outcomes ($T_1 = R$ with prob $\frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$ and $T_1 = G$ with prob $\frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$) and updates Box 2 contents to 5R, 2G and 4R, 3G respectively.
Sets up total probability for $T_2 = R$: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{5}{7} + \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{7}$.
Evaluates Box 1 composition after Step 2 for all four paths: (R, R) leaves 3R, 3G; (R, G) leaves 2R, 4G; (G, R) leaves 4R, 2G; (G, G) leaves 3R, 3G.

Sets up sum of products for drawing red in Step 3: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{5}{7} \times \frac{3}{6} + \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{7} \times \frac{2}{6} + \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{7} \times \frac{4}{6} + \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{7} \times \frac{3}{6}$.
Identifies the joint probability of $T_1 = R$ and final draw red: $\frac{15}{84} + \frac{4}{84} = \frac{19}{84}$.
Applies Bayes' theorem using denominator from part (b): $\frac{19/84}{44/84}$.
Simplifies to $\frac{19}{44}$ (or $0.432$ to 3 s.f.).
